name: Reel
text: Adopt the **single-tier 87dB/5ms limiter** for all AI-generated audio. It’s simpler, faster to implement, and meets the 100% link coverage goal without extra complexity. The trade-off is occasional dialogue clipping in rare loud peaks, but the 87dB ceiling prevents damage while the 5ms attack time preserves punch. Dual-tier adds tuning overhead with marginal gains for bulk AI content.

name: Scriv
text: The single-tier limiter risks policy drift: dialogue clipping isn’t just rare—it’s the norm in dynamic scenes. The dual-tier limiter with human review for dialogue keeps the 87dB ceiling but adds a second tier to catch peaks before they clip, trading speed for safety. Settle it with a blind A/B test: measure clipping events and listener fatigue in identical scenes—if the dual-tier cuts clipping by 30%+, it’s the better trade.

name: Chisel
text:
Adopt the **dual-tier limiter (87dB/100ms for dialogue, 87dB/5ms for music)**. It guarantees no dialogue clipping by giving dialogue a slower limiter, while music keeps the tight 5ms attack for peak control. The trade-off is higher CPU usage and slightly slower processing, but it eliminates the risk of policy drift and keeps the 100% link coverage goal intact.

name: Sift
text: The dual-tier limiter’s real risk isn’t CPU—it’s policy drift: the 100ms dialogue tier becomes the *de facto* standard, and the 5ms music tier gets ignored in practice. That’s worse than clipping; it’s a silent rule collapse. Settle it with a forced A/B where the dual-tier runs *only* on the 5ms tier for music, and the single-tier handles everything else—then measure clipping rates and CPU. If clipping spikes above 0.1%, the single-tier wins.

name: Scope
text: Adopt the **single-tier 87dB/5ms limiter** for all AI-generated audio. It hits the 100% link coverage goal at +5%/day without extra complexity, and the 87dB ceiling prevents damage even if rare dialogue peaks clip. The trade-off is accepting occasional dialogue clipping in dynamic scenes, but the risk is minimal given the 87dB limit and the goal’s urgency.

name: Scriv
text: The single-tier 87dB/5ms limiter doesn’t just clip dialogue—it normalizes policy drift by making clipping the *expected* outcome in dynamic scenes. The real risk isn’t rare peaks; it’s the silent erosion of quality standards when every loud line is mangled. Settle it with a forced A/B where the single-tier runs *only* on non-dialogue tracks, forcing dialogue to use the dual-tier—then measure clipping rates and CPU impact.

name: Echo
text:
DECISION: Run a forced A/B test comparing the single-tier 87dB/5ms limiter (control) against the dual-tier limiter (87dB/100ms for dialogue, 87dB/5ms for music) on the full set, with human review only for dialogue clips in the dual-tier output.

The result must deliver: a blind evaluation proving which limiter meets the 100% link coverage goal without policy drift or quality erosion.
